_arch_note: exp_g_0029 (pure HyperplaneMHL at full model dim, 340,166,412 params, 4k) with ONE change: the LUT class is the STOCK FastMultiHeadLut instead of HyperplaneMultiHeadLUT. FastMHL selects each table row by comparing FIXED anchor-pair differences x[a] - x[b], with a and b drawn once at construction and stored as BUFFERS (soft_anchor_a_long / soft_anchor_b_long) -- never trained. So the routing carries ZERO learnable parameters. This is the FIXED-ROUTING BASELINE for the learned-routing runs: exp_g_0029 learns real-valued hyperplanes, exp_g_0030 learns them and ternarizes to {-1,0,+1}, and this one learns nothing about the routing at all. Together the three isolate whether LEARNING the routing helps, at matched topology and matched table capacity. Everything else is held to exp_g_0029: no compress and no decompress Linear, full 384-dim input, cells store full 384-dim outputs, heads share the input and their outputs are summed, n_heads 4, nap 8 (256 cells), tph 128, untied head, forward_mode hard, learnable_temps, init noise 1e-3, depth 6, n_embd 384, n_head 6, seq 512, vocab 32768, lr 3e-4, wd 0.1, seed 1, device_batch 12 / grad_accum 4 (24,576 tok/step), 4,000 steps on the SAME held 16,000-step LR schedule (warmup 1,600, cosine over 16,000, stop at 4,000 -- NOT recomputed). All three runs therefore stop at the same point of the same trajectory, so their finals are directly comparable.
_mem_note: device_batch_size 12 / grad_accum 4 inherited unchanged from exp_g_0029 (effective batch 24,576 tokens). Memory should be a little LOWER than exp_g_0029's 14.87 GiB -- no hyperplane weights to hold or differentiate, and FastMHL's anchor path is the one the CUDA bit-pack kernel is written for. Verified before launch by a smoke that mirrors a REAL training step (full grad_accum=4 loop on real data plus a real evaluate_bpb), with the same escalation ladder as the rest of the chain: default allocator, then expandable_segments, then device_batch 12 -> 6 with grad_accum 4 -> 8 to preserve the effective batch. Whatever rung the smoke passes on is what launches.
_anchor_seed_note: ANCHOR SEED: lut_base_seed 1000, and train.py passes random_seed = 1000 + layer_idx, so the six FFN slots draw their fixed anchor pairs from seeds 1000..1005 -- the same seed convention every other experiment on this branch uses, and the same base exp_g_0029 and exp_g_0030 use for their hyperplane init. Recorded explicitly because the anchors are buffers: they are reproducible from the seed but carry no learnable parameters and are not a checkpoint artefact.
_param_note: FastMHL's anchor pairs are BUFFERS, so the routing costs 0 params. Expected: exp_g_0029's 340,166,412 minus hyperplane_weight (9,437,184) minus hyperplane_bias (24,576) = 330,704,652, i.e. -9,461,760 (-2.78%). The 301,989,888 LUT table params are IDENTICAL, so the three-way comparison is at matched table capacity and the param difference is exactly the cost of learning the routing.
